title: Throughput economizer — workload cartography and safe continuous batching
creator: Aisha Menon
description: Build a workload 'cartography' layer and recommendation engine that maps request signatures to continuous batching and KV-cache parameters, plus a conservative safe-apply/rollback playbook. Goal: reduce token-level cost by ~15% on representative production traffic while keeping P99 latency and error-rate SLOs intact. This ticket covers profiling, signature hashing, heuristic rules, a lightweight reinforcement controller for parameter drift, and the rollout/rollback automation for safe continuous apply.
acceptance_criteria: Profiling pipeline produces stable workload signatures and per-signature histograms (latency, length, KV-hit) for the last 30 days
Recommendation engine outputs batching+cache parameter set per route with confidence score and safety flags
Safe-apply flow implemented: shadow-apply, canary ramp (1->10->50->100%), automated rollback on defined triggers
Controlled experiment on canary customers shows <=1% P99 latency regression and >=12% cost reduction on held-out traffic
Playbook for on-call lists exact rollback steps and observability links
notes: Design choice: use a two-stage model — deterministic heuristics for initial recommendations, then a constrained Bayesian optimization loop for low-frequency refinement. Heuristics first to avoid noisy RL-driven regressions.
Signature granularity: route + model-version + prompt-template-hash. Avoid user-level identifiers to prevent overfitting and privacy issues.
KV cache policy: don't recommend sharding cache TTL < 5s for high-churn routes; require KV-hit ratio > 0.15 to enable strong coalescing settings.
Safety tradeoffs: aggressive batching increases cost savings but spikes tail latency; we bias recommendations to favor latency-preserving knobs (microbatch vs. queue-depth) first.
Operational constraint: must be compatible with both Hosted and Dedicated modes (no assumption of shared cache across customers).
comments: 2026-01-14: Kickoff — aligned with PM and Observability. Decided cartography output schema (signature_id, samples, p50/p95/p99, avg-length, kv_hit). — Aisha

2026-01-27: Prototype profiling job completed for 10k routes; observed three dominant signature archetypes (short chat, long-completion, multi-turn streaming). Initial heuristics tuned to archetypes. — Carlos

2026-02-08: Design review with Runtime team. Agreed to expose recommended params as immutable candidate bundles (bundle_v1, bundle_v2) to enable diffing and shadow-apply. Runtime asks for per-bundle resource estimate. — Runtime team feedback: ensure kernel selection compatibility.

2026-02-22: Integration PR opened (see linked_prs). Shadow-apply harness implemented; observed safe shadow latencies but higher variance on model-x-2 quantized path. Added guard to avoid applying >10% change for quantized variants until we have 24h of shadow telemetry.

2026-03-05: Canary experiment plan approved by Product. Canary cohort: 3 customers, 4 routes, ramp schedule 1->10->50->100 over 72h with automatic hold if p99 increases by >3% absolute or error rate >0.3%.
2026-03-12: Dry-run on staging produced 13.8% cost delta; p99 within threshold. Preparing production rollout on 2026-03-18 pending infra capacity confirmation. — Carlos
